questions.q:
Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct?

(A) The $pH$~of $1 \times {10}^{– 8}MHCl$~solution is $8$.

(B) The conjugate base of ${H}_{2}{PO}^{4 -}$ is ${HPO}_{4}^{2 -}$.

(C) ${K}_{w}$ increases with increase in temperature.

(D) When a solution of a weak monoprotic acid is titrated against a strong base at half neutralisation point,~$pH = \dfrac{1}{2}{pK}_{a}$. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
When concentration of& $H^{+}$~ion is more than~${10}^{- 7}M$, the proton concentration from water must be considered. Hence, the pH of~${10}^{- 8}MHCl$~solution is not equal to 8.

$\mathop{{H}_{2}{PO}_{4}^{-}}_{Acid}\overset{}{⇌}\mathop{HPO42 -}_{Conjugatebase} + H^{+}$

${K}_{w}$ increase with increase in temperature as dissociation of water increases with increase in temperature.

When weak monoprotic acid is titrated against strong base, at half neutralization point, the solution becomes acidic buffer and its $pH$ is given by

$pH = {pK}_{a} + log \left[Salt\right] \left[$Acid\right]$

$⇒ pH = {pK}_{a} + 0$~as \left[salt\right] = \left[acid\right]$

questions.q: pH of water is 7 at $25^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}} \mathrm{C}$. If water is heated to $80^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}} \mathrm{C}$., it's pH will :
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
At $25^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}} \mathrm{C}$, pure water has $\mathrm{pH}=7$
As temperature increased, water molecules dissociate more into hydrogen ions ( $\mathrmH^{+}$) and hydroxide ions  \left(\mathrm{OH}^{-}\right)$.
This increased dissociation leads to slightly decrease in pH .
At $80^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}} \mathrm{C}, \mathrm{pH} \approx 6.93$

questions.q: $20ml$ of ${0.1 M H}_{2}{SO}_{4}$ solution is added to $30mL$ of $0 .2 M{NH}_{4}OH$ solution. The $pH$ of the resultant mixture is:  \left[{pk}_{b}of{NH}_{4}OH = 4 .7\right]$
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Millimoles of ${H}_{2}S{O}_{4} = 20 \times 0.1 = 2$

Millimoles of $N{H}_{4}OH = 30 \times 0.2 = 6$



Hence, the solution will act as a basic buffer.

$pOH = p{K}_{b} + log\dfrac{\left[salt\right]}{\left[Base\right]}$

\left[N{H}_{4}^{+}\right] = 2 \times \left[{\left(N{H}_{4}\right)}_{2}S{O}_{4}\right]; {\left[N{H}_{4}\right]}^{+} = 4$

$pOH = p{K}_{b} + log\dfrac{\left[N{H}_{4}^{+}\right]}{\left[N{H}_{3}\right]}$

$= 4.7 + log\dfrac{4}{2}$

$= 4.7 + 0.3010 = 5.010$

$pH = 14 - pOH = 9$

$

questions.q: The $pH$ of a $0.02MN{H}_{4}Cl$ solution will be [Given:~${K}_{b}\left(N{H}_{4}OH\right) = {10}^{- 5}$ and $log ⁡ 2 = 0.301$]
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
$N{H}_{4}Cl$ is a salt of a strong acid and a weak base.

$pH = \dfrac{1}{2} \left({pK}_{w} - {pK}_{b} -logC\right)$

$= $\dfrac{1}{2} \left[14 - 5 - log ⁡ 2 \times {10}^{- 2}\right]$

$= $\dfrac{1}{2} \left[9 - log ⁡ 2 - log ⁡ {10}^{- 2}\right]$

$= \dfrac{1}{2} \left[9 - log ⁡ 2 + 2\right]$

$= \dfrac{10.7}{2} = 5.35$

questions.q: The solubility of $AgCN$~in a buffer solution of $pH = 3$~is $x$. The value of $x$ is: [Assume : No cyano complex is formed ; ${K}_{sp}\left(AgCN\right) = 2 . 2 \times {10}^{- 16}$ and ${K}_{a}\left(HCN\right) = 6 . 2 \times {10}^{- 10}$]
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Let, the solubility be& $x$

Given that,~

~${K}_{sp}\left(AgCN\right) = 2 . 2 \times {10}^{- 16}$ and ${K}_{a}\left(HCN\right) = 6 . 2 \times {10}^{- 10}$

$AgCN ⇌ \mathop{Ag +}_{x} + \mathop{CN -}_{x}{K}_{sp} = 2 . 2 \times {10}^{- 16}$

$H^{+} + {CN}^{-} ⇌ HCNK = \dfrac{1}{{K}_{a}} = \dfrac{1}{6 . 2 \times {10}^{- 10}}$

${K}_{sp} \times \dfrac{1}{{K}_{a}} = \left[{Ag}^{+}\right]\left[{CN}^{-}\right] \times \dfrac{[ HCN ]}{\left[H^{+}\right]\left[{CN}^{-}\right]}$

$2 . 2 \times {10}^{- 16} \times \dfrac{1}{6 . 2 \times {10}^{- 10}} = \dfrac{[ S ] [ S ]}{10- 3}$

$S^{2} = \dfrac{2 . 2}{6 . 2} \times {10}^{- 9}$

$S^{2} = 3 . 55 \times {10}^{- 10}$

$S = \sqrt{3 . 55 \times {10}^{- 10}}$

$S = 1 . 88 \times {10}^{- 5} ⇒ 1 . 9 \times {10}^{- 5}$

questions.q: The Plot of $pH$-metric titration of weak base ${NH}_{4}OH$ vs strong acid $HCl$ looks like
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Titration curve of ${NH}_{4}OH$ vs~$HCl \left(WB\right) \left(+$SA\right)$

At the very beginning of the curve, the pH starts by falling quite quickly as the acid is added, but the curve very soon gets less steep. This is because a buffer solution is being set up composed of the excess ammonium hydroxide& and the ammonium chloride being formed.

Notice that the equivalence point is now somewhat acidic ( a bit less than pH 5), because pure ammonium chloride isn't neutral. However, the equivalence point still falls on the steepest bit of the curve.& That will turn out to be important in choosing a suitable indicator for the titration.

For the above titration the indicator suitable is methyl orange

$

questions.q: In an acid-base titration, $0.1MHCl$ solution was added to the $NaOH$ solution of unknown strength. Which of the following correctly shown the change of $pH$ of the titration mixture in this experiment?
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
For titration of strong base with strong acid $pH$ changes sharply near equivalence point and at equivalent point $pH$ sharply decreases because strong base & strong acid dissociate completely.
$\overset{SA}{HCl} + \overset{SB}{NaOH} \to NaCl + {H}_{2}O\left(l\right)$
at equivalent point $pH = 7$ and at endpoint solution will be neutral.

questions.q: ${K}_{a}$ for ${CH}_{3}COOH$ is $1 . 8 \times {10}^{- 5}$ and ${K}_{b}$ for ${NH}_{4}OH$ is $1 . 8 \times {10}^{- 5} .$ The $pH$ of ammonium acetate solution will be
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
${K}_{a}$ of ${CH}_{3}COOH= 1 . 8 \times {10}^{- 5}$

${K}_{a}$ of ${NH}_{4}OH= 1 . 8 \times {10}^{- 5}$

We know that $pH$ of solution of the salt made up of weak acid \left({CH}_{3}COOH\right)$ and weak base \left({NH}_{4}OH\right)$ can be found using formula

$pH = 7 + \dfrac{1}{2} \left[{pK}_{a} - {pK}_{b}\right]$

${pK}_{a} = - log \left({K}_{a}\right)
$= - $log\left($1 . 8 $\times {10}^{- 5}\right) = - \left[$log1 . 8 + log{10}^{- 5}\right] = - \left[$0 . 2553 - 5\right] = + 4 . 7447{pK}_{b} = - $log\left({K}_{b}\right) = --log\left(1 . 8 \times {10}^{- 5}\right) =4 . 7447pH = 7 + $\dfrac{1}{2}\left[$4 . 7447 - 4 . 7447\right] = 7 + 0 = 7$

If ${K}_{a} = {K}_{b}$, then $pH$ of salt is always $7$.
Therefore, the $pH$ of given solution is $7$.

$
